title: SeeQ: Training Generalist Value Functions for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
summary: SeeQ trains a vision-language Q-function to score actions for the currently active subtask rather than the full long-horizon robot task, turning sparse, delayed rewards into shorter TD learning problems. It uses subtask annotations in offline manipulation data during training, then predicts the active subtask autoregressively in natural language at test time before estimating value. Pretrained on diverse open-source robot data and finetuned downstream, it improves best-of-N policy steering across four real-world bimanual manipulation tasks on two robot platforms.

extra.full_text: Despite rapid progress, generalist robot policies remain brittle on complex, long-horizon tasks that comprise multiple stages or require repeated attempts and deliberation on the same underlying stage before success. Q-value functions can improve these policies by ranking candidate actions or guiding policy improvement, but learning from sparse task-level rewards entails long credit-assignment horizons, difficult Bellman backups, and broad data-coverage requirements. We introduce SeeQ (Subtask-elicited Q-functions), which instead learns Q-values for the currently active subtask. This shortens the value-prediction horizon and enables effective learning with temporal-difference (TD) objectives. During training, subtask-level annotations present in offline robot data provide the decomposition and enable learning from broad, potentially suboptimal robot datasets. To eliminate the need for human annotations or modular subtask prediction systems at test time, our Q-function architecture is trained to autoregressively predict the active subtask in natural language before estimating its value. We instantiate SeeQ using a base vision-language backbone, pretrain it on diverse open-source robot manipulation data, and finetune it on downstream tasks. Across four real-world manipulation tasks on two bimanual robot platforms, the SeeQ value function substantially improves best-of-N policy steering.

title: Boston Dynamics Opens Robotics Metaplant Application Center to Train Humanoid Robots for Manufacturing Tasks
summary: Boston Dynamics has opened a robotics application center inside Hyundai Motor Group’s Metaplant America campus near Savannah, Georgia, where Atlas humanoid robots are being trained for manufacturing tasks. The facility is meant to turn Atlas from a research platform into a deployable industrial robot, with Hyundai already planning to broaden the training scope and move the effort into a larger site in 2027.

title: Lain-Ego0/LainLab
summary: LainLab is a robot reinforcement-learning pipeline that spans simulation validation and deployment across robots from multiple vendors, using mjlab 1.6.0 as its base. It looks aimed at teams that need a common workflow for training policies, checking them in simulation, and moving them toward real robot deployment rather than maintaining separate stacks for each platform.

extra.full_text: LainLab is a reinforcement-learning, simulation-validation, and deployment project for robots from multiple vendors, built on mjlab 1.6.0.

title: CodeMidas: Scaling Agentic Coding RL Environments from Code Itself
summary: CodeMidas turns existing implemented functionality in open-source codebases into executable RL training environments without relying on issues, commits, or other development artifacts. Its agents inspect code to infer behavioral specs, build execution-grounded tests from the original implementation, and filter tasks through validation and repeated solution rollouts, yielding 5,545 tasks from 3,185 repositories across 23 languages. Training MiMo-V2.5 with GRPO on these tasks improves results across five benchmarks, including +11.7% on DeepSWE, +17% on ProgramBench, and +8.5% on Terminal-Bench v2.1, with analysis showing more codebase exploration and more varied self-verification.

extra.full_text: Training capable coding agents via reinforcement learning (RL) requires diverse tasks with reliable verifiers. Open-source codebases offer a rich source of such tasks, while existing methods typically rely on development artifacts such as issues and commits, limiting the range of tasks that can be extracted. To better scale RL environments, we present CodeMidas, an agentic pipeline that turns implemented functionality in existing codebases into executable RL environments using source code as its only task-specific input. CodeMidas allocates agentic compute to every stage of environment construction: agents explore implemented functionality to formulate behavioral specifications, construct tests grounded in execution of the original code, and validate and filter candidate tasks through execution checks and repeated solution rollouts. The resulting dataset has 5,545 training tasks from 3,185 open-source codebases spanning 23 programming languages and 15 technical domains. Training MiMo-V2.5 on these tasks with GRPO improves performance on all five diverse benchmarks, covering issue repair (DeepSWE + 11.7%), whole-program construction (ProgramBench +17%), and terminal work (Terminal-Bench v2.1 +8.5%). Ablations show that increasing the number of high-quality training tasks improves performance. Trajectory analysis shows the RL-trained agent demonstrates better behaviors like increasing codebase exploration and more diverse self-verification. These results establish source code as a scalable foundation for constructing RL environments that improve coding agents across diverse software tasks.

summary: ETRI says it helped launch ITU-T’s Focus Group on Embodied AI, the first dedicated physical-AI standardization group within a formal international standards body, and secured leadership roles including vice chair and working-group chair positions. The effort matters because it puts Korean researchers near the center of defining common rules for AI systems that perceive, decide, and act in the physical world, from robots and vehicles to factories.

title: Construction Robotics Gains Commercial Momentum in India as Pace Robotics Scales Deployment
summary: Pace Robotics is moving its Centa Painter construction robot from demos and pilots into commercial deployment on live construction sites in India. The news signals that construction robotics there is beginning to find practical traction, especially for repetitive finishing work like painting where automation can improve consistency and reduce dependence on scarce skilled labor.

title: ABB Robotics E-Device simplifies robot interaction on customers' own devices
summary: ABB Robotics introduced E-Device, a way to operate, program, and monitor OmniCore-powered robots and cobots from a customer’s own tablet or PC rather than a dedicated teach pendant. The point is to make robot deployment and day-to-day interaction easier with a consistent interface across ABB systems, while retaining integrated safety controls and ISO 10218:2025 compliance.

summary: Unitree introduced the Dex5-S, a biomimetic dexterous robot hand with 22 degrees of freedom in a 1:1 human-hand form factor, priced from $6.5K before tax and shipping. title: Military milestone: Ukrainian naval drone sinks Russian kamikaze drone boat
summary: A Ukrainian naval drone reportedly sank a Russian kamikaze drone boat in the Black Sea, marking a rare drone-on-drone engagement at sea. The incident matters because both sides are increasingly using unmanned surface vessels to threaten ports, shipping, and naval assets, turning the Black Sea into a testing ground for autonomous and remotely operated maritime warfare.

summary: Seoul selected 28 foreign master’s students in science and engineering for its 2026 Seoul Tech Scholarship, targeting fields such as AI, robotics, bio, quantum technology, fintech, and creative industries. summary: SoftBank Group has reportedly agreed to acquire Hyundai Motor Group’s Robotics and AI Institute, with the deal now under review by the U.S. Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States. title: RS South Africa Supports Next-Generation Edge Artificial Intelligence (AI) With NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano 2
summary: RS South Africa has launched support for NVIDIA’s Jetson Orin Nano 2, a compact robotics computer aimed at edge AI systems for intelligent machines, robotics, and vision workloads. The announcement matters because it points to more capable on-device perception and inference in small robotic platforms, where low-latency processing near sensors is often more useful than sending data back to the cloud.

summary: KITECH has appointed senior advisor Son Woong-hee as its 14th president, with a three-year term running from September 22, 2026 to September 21, 2029. title: 55개국 958개팀 몰린 ‘수학 두뇌 대결’... LG CNS, 최적화 경진대회 성료
summary: LG CNS concluded its 2026 Optimization Grand Challenge, Korea’s only mathematical optimization competition, with 958 teams from 55 countries participating. The contest highlights growing interest in optimization methods that search huge combinatorial spaces for efficient solutions, a capability increasingly central to AI, quantum computing, robotics, and other next-generation industrial systems.

extra.full_text: LG CNS(대표 현신균)가 국내 유일의 수학적최적화(Mathematical Optimization) 경연대회 '최적화 그랜드 챌린지 2026'을 마무리하고 시상식을 열었다고 21일 밝혔다.수학적최적화는 주어진 자원과 조건 안에서 나올 수 있는 방대한 경우의 수를 따져 가장 효율적인 답을 찾아내는 기술이다. 인공지능과 양자컴퓨팅, 로봇 등 차세대 산업을 뒷받침하는 핵심 기반 기술로 꼽힌다. LG CNS는 이 분야의 저변을 넓히기 위해 2024년부터 대한산업공학회와 함께 매년 대회를 열고 있다.올해는 참가 규모가 눈에 띄게 커졌다.
